description: Granular reconstitution of a soundfile, pinned to submode 2 (TIMESTRETCH). Reads the input at a velocity (re)scaled relative to the output, producing time-stretching or compression with a granular character. The program 'modify brassage' has seven internal sub-modes — this entry curates submode 2 only. Other sub-modes (PITCHSHIFT, REVERB, SCRAMBLE, GRANULATE, BRASSAGE proper, FULL MONTY) can be added as separate curated entries post-Phase 1a.
musical_use: Time-stretch or compress source material at its original pitch — pitch is retained throughout, unlike modify speed — while imparting a granular grain. velocity < 1 stretches (slows down), velocity > 1 compresses (speeds up). velocity = 0 is a special 'infinite stretch' case that requires the -loutlength flag (not exposed in this entry).

velocity.description: Speed of advance in the infile relative to the outfile. Inverse of timestretch factor: 0.5 doubles duration, 2.0 halves it. Must be >= 0; the zero case is degenerate without -loutlength.

examples.description: Stretch a source to double its duration with granular character.
examples.expected_use: Granular time-stretch of a short sound (e.g. frog vocalization) into a longer textural gesture.

known_issues: velocity = 0 produces infinite stretch and requires the -loutlength flag, which this curated entry does not expose. Use a small positive velocity instead.
